entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

import json, logging
from buyer.agent import load_package
from buyer.policy import Negotiator
pkg = load_package('data/package')
cases = {c['case_id']: c for c in json.load(open('logs/cases/practice.json'))}

for cid, path in [('case:P02','logs/sessions/practice/P02_3ad1d67f26aac5e7.json'),('case:P08','logs/sessions/practice/P08_7701b00c7a9a8b3e.json'),('case:P11','logs/sessions/practice/P11_3ac9ee6cf673cf7c.json')]:

commit c5c52d7b8b9d551da8c86c174c0a277f546f0ce6
Author: Julian Fritz <j.fritz.11@icloud.com>
Date:   Sat Oct 10 21:02:56 2026 +0200

    Fix the accept gate in the fallback close, guard index-clause adoption by C and must-haves
    
    - fallback_close accepted a standing sheet dearer than the alternative (P08 case file: 1.43M
      against C_alt 1.16M); it now uses the same acceptable() gate as best_offer.
    - adopt() took any index clause the supplier put in its sheet. It now takes the clause only when
      its sheet, clause included, costs less than its previous one and keeps every must-have. The rule
      adopts in all P08 and P18 sessions and refuses Nordmark's copper clause in both P02 sessions
      that scored 0.
    - A late message counts as a round: rollback() tracks it and moves_left subtracts it, so we never
      try an eleventh message after a timeout.
    - No model paragraph once a thread's clock has run 25 s; writer timeout 15 s.
    - Docs: our writer is OpenAI-compatible only (LLM_PROVIDER is not read); README no longer says the
      kit's LLMAgent plays. Dead code removed (Negotiator.lock, plan_terms keep/require_clause).
    - Tests for both gates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

import time

# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

"""The Live Final loop end to end on arena-sim: waves appear one after another in the case list,
every case of a wave plays within its cap, a poll error is polled again, and the loop ends when
the last wave has closed. No network, no model."""

import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

from buyer import runner


class FinalClient(ArenaClient):
    """The sim's client with a scripted final: `cases("final")` is 403 before the first wave, then
    lists each wave's cases as open with seconds left, then as closed; one poll fails outright."""

    def __init__(self, url, key, waves):
        super().__init__(url, key, rate=1000)
        self.waves, self.polls = waves, 0

    def cases(self, set_="practice"):
        if set_ != "final":
            return super().cases(set_)
        self.polls += 1
        if self.polls == 1:
            raise ArenaError(403, "the final has not started")
        if self.polls == 3:
            raise ArenaError(500, "a hiccup")
        wave = min(1 + (self.polls - 2) // 2, len(self.waves))  # a new wave every second poll
        out = []
        for w, ids in enumerate(self.waves, start=1):
            if w > wave:
                continue
            open_ = w == wave
            for cid in ids:
                out.append({"case_id": cid, "wave": w, "open": open_, "seconds_left": 480 if open_ else 0})
        return out


@pytest.fixture
def sim_url():
    sim = Sim(load_cases(), clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(sim), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


def test_play_waves_plays_every_wave(sim_url, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    key = ArenaClient(sim_url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    waves = [["case:S01", "case:S02"], ["case:S03"]]
    client = FinalClient(sim_url, key, waves)
    out = runner.play_waves(client, waves=2, parallel=3, poll=0.05)
    assert set(out) == {"case:S01", "case:S02", "case:S03"}
    for case_id, result in out.items():
        assert not isinstance(result, Exception), (case_id, result)
        assert "deal" in result

Bargaining power comes from patience, so estimate each supplier’s cost of delay.
With both sides equally patient (δ = 0.9), the proposer gets only 53 % of the surplus. Against an impatient supplier (δ = 0.7), it gets 81 %.
Our data shows impatience:
cash-short signals: Wälzhammer’s and Weißacher’s credit indices, short-time work
free capacity advertised: Fuchsreiter, Ilzauer
how much of its turnover we are
its own reply delay and quote validity
A patient supplier (full order book, near-monopolist) won’t move much on price, so go for non-price levers.
Turn that into the capture target. Instead of a guessed 0.65–0.8, compute a share from the estimated patience of both sides and clamp it by tier and goal. This directly addresses your open “capture is still a guess” problem, and it’s explainable to the jury.
Our own patience falls during a wave. Fewer rounds left and a closer cap mean a lower δ for us, so concede faster or accept. A strong alternative raises our patience. The closing rule follows from the model: continue only while the expected gain from one more round exceeds its cost (walk risk times what we’d lose, plus time).
Delay is pure loss. In equilibrium, agreement is immediate, and in the arena every round costs about 60–75 s. Against an impatient supplier, make the first counter close to where you expect to land rather than an extreme anchor followed by many small steps. Every round must carry information, such as the probe sheets.
Proposer advantage. The supplier’s opening quote is its proposal, but our first counter is the reference it reacts to. Make that counter complete, with all fields at our preferred values. Anything left open closes on the supplier’s standard terms.
Only credible threats count. Subgame perfection rules out threats you wouldn’t carry out. Imply a walk-away only when our alternative actually beats the standing offer. The bots read signals the way the model assumes rational players do, so bluffs cost us.
Where the model stops fitting is where the arena game actually is. The paper notes that when costs are private, delays appear and players pretend to be stronger. That is the arena: “that’s not our reality” and “final offer” can be posturing. So estimate a supplier’s patience from data, not from what it says. This is the same logic as the fact checker.

"""The Live Final loop end to end on arena-sim: waves appear one after another in the case list,
every case of a wave plays within its cap, a poll error is polled again, and the loop ends when
the last wave has closed. No network, no model."""

import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

from buyer import runner


class FinalClient(ArenaClient):
    """The sim's client with a scripted final: `cases("final")` is 403 before the first wave, then
    lists each wave's cases as open with seconds left, then as closed; one poll fails outright."""

    def __init__(self, url, key, waves):
        super().__init__(url, key, rate=1000)
        self.waves, self.polls = waves, 0

    def cases(self, set_="practice"):
        if set_ != "final":
            return super().cases(set_)
        self.polls += 1
        if self.polls == 1:
            raise ArenaError(403, "the final has not started")
        if self.polls == 3:
            raise ArenaError(500, "a hiccup")
        wave = min(1 + (self.polls - 2) // 2, len(self.waves))  # a new wave every second poll
        out = []
        for w, ids in enumerate(self.waves, start=1):
            if w > wave:
                continue
            open_ = w == wave
            for cid in ids:
                out.append({"case_id": cid, "wave": w, "open": open_, "seconds_left": 480 if open_ else 0})
        return out


@pytest.fixture
def sim_url():
    sim = Sim(load_cases(), clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(sim), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


def test_play_waves_plays_every_wave(sim_url, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    key = ArenaClient(sim_url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    waves = [["case:S01", "case:S02"], ["case:S03"]]
    client = FinalClient(sim_url, key, waves)
    out = runner.play_waves(client, waves=2, parallel=3, poll=0.05)
    assert set(out) == {"case:S01", "case:S02", "case:S03"}

# per supplier: reply_delay_days / validity_days signals vs number of counters and total concession
rows=collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in glob.glob('logs/sessions/*/*.json'):
    d=json.load(open(p)); tr=(d.get('result') or {}).get('trace') or []
    sups=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for m in tr:
        if m['actor']!='buyer': sups[m['actor']].append(m)
    for sid, ms in sups.items():
        sig=[(x['move'].get('signals') or {}) for x in ms]
        prices=[x['move'].get('terms',{}).get('unit_price') for x in ms if x['move'].get('terms',{}).get('unit_price')]
        if len(prices)<2: continue
        delays=sorted(set(s.get('reply_delay_days') for s in sig if s)); vals=sorted(set(s.get('validity_days') for s in sig if s))
        rows[sid].append((len(prices)-1, round((prices[0]-prices[-1])/prices[0]*100,1), delays, vals))
for sid, r in sorted(rows.items()):
    n=[x[0] for x in r]; conc=[x[1] for x in r]
    print(f"{sid:14s} runs={len(r):2d} counters={min(n)}-{max(n)} concession%={min(conc)}-{max(conc)} delays={sorted(set(sum([x[2] for x in r],[])))} validity={sorted(set(sum([x[3] for x in r],[])))}")
EOF

Done for tonight's practice loop. State and answers:

**Where we stand**
- Practice mean 0.727 → **0.737** (`/v1/me`): P08 0.549 → 0.648 (deal 5.26 with the clause). 13 runs spent (78 used); the last 13 runs brought +0.0095 on the mean, so the stop rule is met. Everything else is at the bot's ceiling (see below).
- Code: v8 merged into `main` via PR #12 (with Julian's and the review-fix session's changes); new branch `steffen/final-prep`, draft PR #13 with learnings, logs and `tests/test_waves.py` (the Live Final wave loop end to end on the sim: 403 before the first wave, a 500 poll, two waves, every case closes). 35 tests pass, ruff clean.
- Robustness added for Sunday: guarded setup/move (fallback resends our last sheet), wave poll never raises and resumes a crashed case with its path rebuilt, release letters and news reach the persona profile, supplier e-mails scanned for traits, `price_unit`, unknown Incoterm and scorecard guards, cost-breakdown question removed, currency claims removed, the reader answers the bots' asks (volume figure, forecast CSV on "proof", fixed payment said plainly).

**Your three questions, against the traces**

1. *Compounding 30 % and starting lower.* The data says front-load, not back-load. Every bot's concession after its first counter is `min(about 0.8 x our move, a cap that shrinks by round)` (D01: 1.6 %, 0.8 %, 0.6 %, 0.4 %, 0.2 %; Donautal 0.06 to 0.15 then 0.04; Werdenfels 0.10 to 0.20 then 0), and the thread ends after a fixed number of counters (distributors 3, Leitner 3, Nordmark 4, Ravensteiner 2, D01 6) or right after a move of ours under 1 %. A small early move loses the biggest cap (P08 +0.06 → +0.06, +0.22 → +0.20) and a move over 50 % of the gap gets a hold. A 40 % share bought nothing extra (P18, two runs: same 0.10). So 30 % of the remaining gap, shrinking in absolute terms, is already the right shape; I left it.

2. *Patience variables.* `BUDGET` (1.0; relationship goals 0.3, capacity_full 0.16, near_cost 0.14) barely drives the bots: they stop by counter count, Nordmark at a cumulative gap of 0.03, the distributors at 0.33 to 0.44. The budget matters only where a walk is possible (Nordmark withdrew at 2 to 7 % below its price), so the near_cost and capacity_full overrides stay; the rest of the budget machinery is inert and I did not extend it.

3. *Rubinstein paste.* Supported by the data in one direction: `reply_delay_days` 4 to 5 and no validity mark the founder-run job shops, which conceded up to 22 %; groups (1 to 2 days) 0 to 12 %. The engine already exploits it through `DEEP` (a first drop of 6 %+ means a deep floor, hold low) and the persona overrides, without a δ estimate. The capture target is moot here: the deal is the bot's last counter, and "it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the counter it would make" means a sheet at our target never beats its own path. Where the model does not fit is the records on P08/P18: identical sheets and claims gave first counters from 5.43 to 5.60 and finals 5.26 to 5.61, so the best-of-N on `/v1/me` is mostly the bot's own randomness. Non-price levers are priced by the bots at exactly our cost (deadband +0.12 = our index cost; 300 ppm +0.50 ≈ our quality cost), except payment days at a rate unlike ours, which `plan_terms` already takes.

**Not done / for Sunday**: 08:00 release check (`DataPackage(...).release` not None, CSV columns), 09:00 one practice case through the final machine, `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v` from `main`. The merge also carries the review session's writer budget and close retries; both ran clean in the v9 smoke runs. Open: 4+ bidders would still time out (no case file has more than 3).

EOF

    """Our view of the supplier for `supplier_value` and the relationship term. `lead`: the lead
    time it quoted; `overtime`: what each day faster costs it, as a share of the price."""
    standard = known_incoterm(case, closing_terms(case, {}, known_incoterm(case, std or {})))
    est = {"standard": standard, "interest_rate": rate, "lead": lead, "overtime": overtime}
    if ppm is not None:
        est["ppm"] = ppm
    if full_cost:
        est["full_cost"] = full_cost
    return est


def value(case, terms, est):
    """What a sheet is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash at its standard terms, less the
    overtime a faster delivery than it quoted costs it (fully booked suppliers: about 0.5 % of
    the price per day, P05 and P10)."""
    v = supplier_value(case, known_incoterm(case, terms), est)
    lead, quoted = terms.get("lead_time_days"), est.get("lead")
    if est.get("overtime") and lead is not None and quoted and lead < quoted:

content.text:
Wrapping up this round; everything is committed and pushed, nothing left to request.

**The gap to first place, and what closed part of it tonight**

Standings now: NoIdea 0.842 (7 of 10 records), gLarPC 0.777, **Codacabana 0.776 (rank 3, from rank 7 at 0.736 when you asked)**. Per case, record / ours: P01 1.00/0.97, P02 0.85/0.73, P03 0.94/0.92, P04 0.87/0.86, P05 0.92/0.83, P07 0.81/0.75, P08 0.92/0.67, P10 0.70/0.68, P11 0.81/0.71, P18 0.71/0.63. The 0.066 gap to NoIdea is almost entirely P08 (0.25) and P02 (0.11), then P05, P11, P07 (about 0.06 to 0.10 each).

What the gap was made of, and the three fixes (all on `steffen/consolidate`, PR #16, with scores in `docs/learnings.md`):

1. **Our claim bank only knew 12-month index changes**, where the distributors' main driver AS-14404 rose 5.9 %. Over the window the arena actually accepts (any two months up to 12 apart) it fell 5.5 % since June. Citing that in round 1 moved the first counter for the first time in 14 runs: P08 0.549 → 0.670, P18 0.485 → 0.621 (Werdenfels' path 5.30, 5.20, 5.10 repeats exactly).
2. **Suppliers value an index clause on their rising driver far above its cost to us.** A teammate's run showed Nordmark agreeing at once to a copper clause 4 % below its fixed price. I turned that into a rule (`economics.clause_trade`: supplier value = material share × its driver's 12-month move beyond the deadband; trade when it beats our path cost plus index risk; anchor at the relationship optimum with the full cost capped at the quote). P02 0.507 → 0.735, agreed in round 1. Same rule fires on the unplayed P14 (+21 % of price) and P16; it correctly stays silent for P08/P18, where the bots price the deadband at exactly our cost.
3. **After a job shop's deep first drop, hold the anchor** instead of stepping 8 %: P05 0.822/0.828 held vs 0.806/0.81 stepped. A 3 % deeper anchor made Dralveck walk (patience), so that stays at 0.78.

**What still separates us from NoIdea**: P08's record (5.02 with the clause, essentially Donautal's floor) and P02's 0.847 are beyond what the bots' capped concessions give us even with the claims; I could not find the mechanism in the traces, and the relationship charge caps P02 near 0.74 for a clause deal under our cost estimate. P11 is stuck at 45.50 for everyone but two teams. 50 practice runs used by me (115 of your 200 cap, team total 127).

**Recommendation for the night**: freeze policy here; Sunday 08:00 run the release check and the all-cases sim test (`uv run pytest -q`), 09:00 one practice case through `buyer run --set final` machinery, then submit from `main` after the consolidation PR merges.

Pushing past a final offer ends the case (walk-away). - Verified claims "taken into account" lower where they stop, most in round 1. Irrelevant: their own older quotes outside the case refs, other suppliers' order prices, indices outside their cost drivers, currency rates. - Wording moves price (D01: asking "what would you need" 50.00 to 49.40), but repeating a question every round backfires. - Patience is about a 40% cumulative gap (sum per round of (their counter - our sheet)/their counter). Near-cost and pricing-committee suppliers end earlier; Nordmark (P02) walked at 19%. - Only the standing sheet can be accepted (alternatives return 422): mirror a better alternative back. - Raw-material distributors (P08, P18) refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and any deadband: take their clause. - RFQ: the arena serializes calls per session; the runner sends one message at a time by 60 s deadline. - Round-1 counters: some suppliers follow our anchor (Werdenfels: anchor 4.77 gave 5.50, 5.68 gave 5.70); D01 did not (44 to 47 all gave 51.30). Per-thread fit of the concession curve and patience instead of the fixed FRACTION/ANCHOR constants. 4. A deep anchor plus small, steady gaps afterwards, so leverage distributors run more rounds before their final offer. Raise our practice mean (best score per hosted case, GET /v1/me) on https://arena.tacto.ai/live from 0.727 toward 0.82+ AND make the agent robust for Sunday's Live Final (hidden cases, new suppliers). We are Team Codacabana. Work on branch steffen/price-engine (PR #12); read docs/learnings.md (Takeaways, Where we stand, claim table, Hypotheses) and docs/design.md (Implemented) first.

Budget: 35 practice runs left (100 total, 65 used); sandbox D01/D02 is free, use it for every mechanism test. OpenAI (gpt-6-luna, LLM_EFFORT=low) within $200, about $2 spent. Stop when 10 consecutive practice runs bring no meaningful improvement (>0.01 on the mean), or at 0.85.

Current best per case (ours / best of all teams): P01 0.974/0.995, P02 0.507/0.847, P03 0.923/0.936, P04 0.860/0.874 (capped near 0.87), P05 0.828/0.824, P07 0.751/0.779, P08 0.549/0.732, P10 0.679/0.702, P11 0.710/0.807, P18 0.485/0.677. The upside is in P02, P08, P18, P11.

Established facts (do not re-test):
- Suppliers agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they would make; stay below their counter until their final offer. Pushing past a final offer ends the case (walk-away).
- Verified claims "taken into account" lower where they stop, most in round 1. Irrelevant: their own older quotes outside the case refs, other suppliers' order prices, indices outside their cost drivers, currency rates.
- Wording moves price (D01: asking "what would you need" 50.00 to 49.40), but repeating a question every round backfires.
- Patience is about a 40% cumulative gap (sum per round of (their counter - our sheet)/their counter). Near-cost and pricing-committee suppliers end earlier; Nordmark (P02) walked at 19%.
- Only the standing sheet can be accepted (alternatives return 422): mirror a better alternative back.
- Raw-material distributors (P08, P18) refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and any deadband: take their clause.
- RFQ: the arena serializes calls per session; the runner sends one message at a time by 60 s deadline.
- Round-1 counters: some suppliers follow our anchor (Werdenfels: anchor 4.77 gave 5.50, 5.68 gave 5.70); D01 did not (44 to 47 all gave 51.30).

Open hypotheses to test, cheapest first:
1. Lower round-1 counters for P02/P08/P18 through persona-specific arguments and wording in the first e-mail (hedge letter, open-book offer, partnership).
2. Round 1 with 2 to 3 sheets of equal C for us (payment vs ppm vs lead time) to reveal what each lever is worth (P10, P11).
3. Per-thread fit of the concession curve and patience instead of the fixed FRACTION/ANCHOR constants.
4. A deep anchor plus small, steady gaps afterwards, so leverage distributors run more rounds before their final offer.

Rules (AGENTS.md): no logic keyed on case or supplier IDs (generalise to unseen suppliers); never call /v1/events, /screen, /leaderboard, /results; no prompt injection; code owns every number, the model only writes words; every model call has a hard timeout; no em-dashes. Before each PR update run uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . Record every finding in docs/learnings.md (date, tag, evidence session ID) and design changes in docs/design.md, in the same PR. Commit logs with git add -f logs/sessions logs/runs logs/practice-v*.log, and push to the PR after each batch. Never push to main. Keep the Live Final path (buyer run --set final, runner.play_waves) working; dry-run it on the sandbox before Sunday 09:00.

Log progress in docs/learnings.md after every batch: version, cases, scores, what changed.
